title: The single-degree layer between two upper truncations
statement:
Let $\mathcal U$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with an arbitrary t-structure $t$ [def-weil-t-structure], and use its truncation functors and counits $\epsilon_r(K):\tau^{\le r}K\to K$ [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. For every $K\in\mathcal U$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, put $C_q(K)=\tau^{\ge q}\tau^{\le q}K$. Then $C_q(K)\in\mathcal U^{\ge q}\cap\mathcal U^{\le q}$, and there are morphisms $u_q,v_q,\delta_q$ giving a distinguished triangle
$$\tau^{\le q-1}K\xrightarrow{u_q}\tau^{\le q}K\xrightarrow{v_q}C_q(K)\xrightarrow{\delta_q}(\tau^{\le q-1}K)[1],$$
where $\epsilon_q(K)\circ u_q=\epsilon_{q-1}(K)$ and $v_q$ is the truncation unit $\tau^{\le q}K\to\tau^{\ge q}\tau^{\le q}K$. No t-bounds on $K$, and no global boundedness or nondegeneracy of $t$, are required.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(ii), paragraph 1.3.4 (nested truncations and extension closure), and Proposition 1.3.5, pp. 29-31 (PDF pp. 30-32): apply the truncation triangle to the upper truncation and identify the nested first vertex.
